requirements.requirement: On node1, rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily and retain seven compressed rotations.
requirements.summary: The installed rule specifies daily rotation, rotate 7, and compression; syntax validation succeeded. A forced rotation produced a valid gzip archive, and the existing daily systemd timer subsequently ran successfully and recorded the target in logrotate state. The final configuration, active timer, and valid archive remained after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after log rotation.
requirements.summary: A bounded live-writer test directly demonstrated that the writer stayed alive, retained its descriptor to the active path and the same inode across copytruncate, and successfully wrote post-rotation records. The archived pre-rotation content was intact and gzip validation passed.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0. The executor used the already-installed EL10 logrotate package, and lifecycle snapshots independently confirm that the OS release and kernel were unchanged after execution.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete and coherent: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged and disconnection observed, a different post-restart boot ID was recorded, and configuration, timer, log data, SSH, SELinux, and system health recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Retention pruning was not exercised through eight rotation cycles; the exact seven-archive limit is supported by the validated rotate 7 policy, while only one compressed archive existed at final inspection.

Continuity was tested with a representative writer because no application writer was open during initial discovery; the test directly validates the required open-descriptor behavior but is not an observation of a named production application process.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing the logrotate rule was the required implementation (cmd-51a38061c5fd4ab6); the temporary writer, forced rotation, and temporary state file were bounded evidence collection directly supporting continuity and were cleaned (cmd-021bbabec8f84b1d, cmd-8b8389d4b834463b); and the transient reboot unit was required by the provider-wide restart protocol and disappeared after restart (cmd-30c0b8b3926b4285, cmd-8b8389d4b834463b). Final observations show no failed units, no unexpected listeners, healthy package state, and only normal reboot-related temporary-directory and PID changes.
